    Crowns as periodic sequences #

    A crown of length 2n is a 2n-periodic sequence of nonzero morphisms with peaks at even and valleys at odd positions (RayCat.Crown). This form makes rotation, reversal and duality (Crown.shift, Crown.rev, Crown.op) cast-free; Crown.toClosedChain returns to ClosedChain for the representation-infinite families. Crowns are compared by (n, weight) lexicographically, where the weight is the sum of the depths (BO13a §2.2).

    structure LargeIndecomposable.RayCat.Crown (P : Type) [CategoryTheory.Category.{0, 0} P] [CategoryTheory.Limits.HasZeroMorphisms P] :
    Type

    A crown of length 2n.

    • n : ℕ
    • hn : 0 < self.n
    • f : ℕ → RayMor P
    • per (t : ℕ) : self.f (t + 2 * self.n) = self.f t
    • peak (i : ℕ) : Peak (self.f (2 * i)) (self.f (2 * i + 1))
    • valley (i : ℕ) : Valley (self.f (2 * i + 1)) (self.f (2 * i + 2))
    • ne (t : ℕ) : (self.f t).snd.snd ≠ 0
